name: Daratumumab
route_note: IV infusion or fixed-dose subcutaneous injection with hyaluronidase; weekly, then every 2 and 4 weeks
owner: Johnson & Johnson (Janssen), under licence from Genmab

discovery.note: Fully human IgG1κ antibody raised in transgenic mice; licensed to Janssen in 2012. Year is the priority date of the Genmab anti-CD38 antibody patent (US 7,829,673).

tagline: First anti-CD38 antibody, now a backbone of multiple myeloma treatment
summary: Daratumumab is a human monoclonal antibody that targets CD38, a glycoprotein highly expressed on myeloma plasma cells. It is combined with lenalidomide, bortezomib, pomalidomide or other agents across all lines of multiple myeloma therapy and is approved for light-chain (AL) amyloidosis.
mechanism: Daratumumab binds CD38 and kills myeloma cells through complement-dependent cytotoxicity, antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and phagocytosis, and by inducing apoptosis after Fc-receptor cross-linking.
It also depletes CD38-positive immunosuppressive cells such as some regulatory T and B cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells, which may enhance T-cell responses.
uses: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (transplant-eligible and ineligible, in combinations)
Light-chain (AL) amyloidosis (with bortezomib, cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone)

history.title: Janssen licence
history.detail: Genmab licenses worldwide rights to Janssen Biotech.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Accelerated approval in November for myeloma after at least three prior lines (GEN501, SIRIUS).

history.title: First-line use
history.detail: Approved with bortezomib, melphalan and prednisone for newly diagnosed transplant-ineligible myeloma.

history.title: Subcutaneous form
history.detail: FDA approves Darzalex Faspro with hyaluronidase, shortening administration to minutes.

history.title: AL amyloidosis
history.detail: Accelerated approval with VCd for newly diagnosed light-chain amyloidosis (ANDROMEDA).

history.title: Quadruplet therapy
history.detail: Approved with bortezomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone for transplant-eligible newly diagnosed myeloma (PERSEUS).

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: Daratumumab binds CD38 on red blood cells and causes positive indirect antiglobulin (Coombs) tests, so patients are typed and screened before starting.
It was the first CD38-targeted antibody approved for myeloma.
